question: Driving the PRODUCT's replenishment logic (lead-time-demand requirement per supplier lead time, coverage-first CP-SAT planner with MOQ, pack multiples, budget and open orders), do the trained forecasters give better simulated inventory outcomes than the seasonal-naive forecaster and than a simple non-forecast base-stock rule under identical constraints?
demand: recorded daily unit sales (fulfilled units; stock-outs in the source are unobserved), lost-sales simulation
event_order: orders are placed at the end of a review day; each day: receive due orders, sell up to stock, record lost units, accrue holding on ending stock

terms.recipe: uci-sim-ops v1 assumption ranges (D-013) applied to every cohort product with a study-only seed; NOT written to the workspace
terms.price_basis: median selling price from sales lines dated before 2011-11-10 (no information after the first review)

initial_stock: ceil(14 x mean daily sales over the 28 days to 2011-11-10), identical for every policy

product_policy.dependence: estimated from recorded selling days up to each review (calendar lags)
product_policy.planner: coverage-first CP-SAT, allow_shortfall true, need_by = review + coverage_days

policies.product_seasonal_naive: product policy fed by seasonal naive
policies.product_lightgbm: product policy fed by LightGBM quantile
policies.product_tcn: product policy fed by quantile TCN seed 0
policies.simple_base_stock: no forecast: S = m (L+C) + z s sqrt(L+C), m and s from the 56 days to the review, z = 1.2816 (90%), per supplier lead time L, same planner
policies.perfect_foresight_reference: requirement = actual sales over (review, review+L+C] minus position, same planner; a reference, not an achievable policy

budgets.workspace_scaled: GBP 20,000 per weekly review per 48 products (the workspace's assumed budget) scaled to the cohort

costs.lost_margin: median selling price minus primary unit cost, floored at 0, per lost unit

metrics: shortfall units reported by the planner
comparisons: per-product total cost differences, product-level paired bootstrap (2,000 resamples): product_tcn and product_lightgbm vs product_seasonal_naive; best product policy vs simple_base_stock
honesty_note: Simulated outcomes on assumed terms and costs; the 28-day window is F1's last test window, already seen by earlier studies, so nothing here is confirmatory. Lower MAE is not assumed to mean lower cost: both are reported side by side.
